summary: When a monster engulfs the mounted hero, C calls dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_ENGULFED) before continuing the engulf transition. JavaScript prints the same plucking message but records steed.c:dismount_steed as unported and skips its landing_spot and steed-release work. The first recorded divergence is the landing_spot random draw at step 253.

source.branch: mhitu.c:gulpmu enters its initial engulf branch, places the engulfer on the hero's square, sets u.ustuck, prints the plucking message, then calls dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_ENGULFED). steed.c:dismount_steed computes landing_spot before checking the steed pointer, accepts DISMOUNT_ENGULFED without a message, releases the steed, chooses an unoccupied adjacent square for it because the hero's square is occupied, avoids float_down for the engulfed reason, and returns to gulpmu.
callers: C mhitu.c:gulpmu:1315 calls steed.c:dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_ENGULFED) after the urgent plucking message. JS js/mhitu.js:gulpmu currently calls note_unported('steed.c dismount_steed') at that site.

C steed.c:dismount_steed:581 initializes have_spot with landing_spot before its null-steed guard; its DISMOUNT_ENGULFED arm proceeds through the common release and occupied-square relocation, then skips float_down. JS js/steed.js:dismount_steed currently throws UnsupportedSteedError for this reason and rejects the occupied hero square.
dependencies: The engulf transition consumes the return from gulpmu and continues the same caller after dismount_steed. Keep the dismount's void contract and preserve its C ordering of landing_spot, u.usteed release, steed relocation, and no float_down.

evidence: The admitted v53 baseline evaluation records this case at 253/359 screens, 3017/3336 RNG calls, and 346/359 cursors. The canonical manifest SHA-256 is fc1feb3315c077db151a113cf6f5c2e1b26ed181b953547e7d3fcf1ad1f51e39 and recording SHA-256 is d684562357a7eb20585e465ef7db1ccd055bb348f09c2a5d7a4301e6b665cc2d.

A bounded replay on commit 3aa063bd0b6fe4e0e36a22c034a4bebae0b7c92d emitted 359 steps with no runtime error. At step 253, C's next RNG call is rn2(3)=0 in steed.c:landing_spot, while JS calls rn2(20)=16; the same step's screen differs at row 1, column 26. The replay log is /tmp/teleport-validation-1000/run-NAUG3V/stdout.log.

Source review of upstream mhitu.c:1315 and steed.c:459-566,575-826 confirms that C invokes the existing dismount helper for every engulfer when the hero rides. JS mhitu.js instead records the helper as unported; JS steed.js separately refuses DISMOUNT_ENGULFED and occupied-square relocation. This is the responsible gap; subsequent RNG calls are downstream.
